scams.name: The Nakasu Girls Bar ¥1,000,000 Overcharge
scams.description: Street touts lure visitors into girls bars in Nakasu where hostesses continuously serve drinks without quoting prices. Bills escalate dramatically—documented cases range from ¥400,000 to over ¥1,000,000 for three hours. Bouncers block exits when customers question charges. Some venues have yakuza affiliations.
scams.avoidance: Never follow street touts into Nakasu venues. Patronize only Google Maps-listed establishments with 4.5+ stars and 50+ English reviews. Demand printed menus with prices before ordering. Leave immediately if seated without pricing information. Call 110 if pressured, citing Fukuoka's Bottakuri Prevention Ordinance.

scams.name: The Nakasu Yatai Foreign-Tourist Overcharge
scams.description: Riverside yatai food stalls systematically overcharge foreign tourists while charging local prices to Japanese customers. A ¥3,200 order becomes ¥5,600. Reviews confirm this targeting pattern is widespread and deliberate, with locals avoiding these tourist-facing stalls.
scams.avoidance: Eat at Tenjin yatai instead, particularly Nagahama. Photograph menus before sitting. Refuse stalls where touts recruited you from the street. Demand itemized receipts before paying. Prioritize stalls with 4.5+ star ratings from Japanese reviewers.
scams.location: Nakasu riverside yatai along Naka River

scams.name: The Hakata Station Tsukushi-guchi Tout Shakedown
scams.description: Organized tout groups operate at Hakata Station's east exit, approaching visitors with low-price drink offers (quoted as ¥3,000) that balloon to ¥15,000–30,000. Touts earn 10–20% commission per customer. Inside venues, unrequested appetizers and service charges are added. Top earners pull ¥500,000 monthly.
scams.avoidance: Use Hakata-guchi (west) exit instead. Ignore all touts—avoid eye contact and engagement. Select restaurants on Google Maps or Tabelog before arriving. Call 110 if pressured. Note that Fukuoka posted anti-tout warning signs at Tsukushi-guchi since 2020.

scams.name: The Tinder / Matching App Bar Lure
scams.description: Users matching on Tinder or Bumble with women who suggest meeting at specific Nakasu or Tenjin bars encounter massive bills (¥40,000–80,000 for minimal drinks and food). The woman is paid per delivered customer and typically vanishes before the bill arrives. Named venues include PIGLET bar on the 3rd floor of Yamamoto Building near Nakasukawabata Station.
scams.avoidance: Insist on venues you select from Google Maps with visible street presence and 4.5+ reviews. Unmatch if she refuses your suggestion. Suggest daytime coffee or walks before drinks. Leave if warning signs appear (upper floor, no signage, she knows staff). Screenshot named problematic venues to pattern-match.
scams.location: Nakasu and Tenjin bars accessed via dating apps

scams.name: The Booking.com 'Cash in the Fridge' Rental Scam
scams.description: Short-term rental hosts demand additional cash payments (¥50,500+) deposited in refrigerators despite full pre-payment through Booking.com. Requests happen via direct messaging outside platform chat. Hosts refuse refunds when guests object. Properties are often in obscure multi-tenant buildings. Pattern reflects unlicensed operations violating Japan's Minpaku Law.
scams.avoidance: Report off-platform payment requests to Booking.com or Airbnb immediately for delisting. Never pay cash outside booking platforms. Initiate credit card chargebacks for unauthorized charges. Report to Fukuoka Police's Hakata-ku division. Prefer hotels with 50+ reviews over apartment rentals for stays.
scams.location: Short-term rentals near Hakata Station (south side)

scams.name: The Hakata Station Phishing Approach
scams.description: Strangers approach visitors at Hakata Station or Fukuoka Airport claiming to represent tourism offices, requesting passport photos for surveys. Phishing harvests passport data and hotel locations for follow-up fraud, fake hotel charges, and identity theft. Variant: unofficial taxis quote flat rates (¥8,000) instead of metered fares (¥1,500), or take circuitous routes to inflate charges.
scams.avoidance: Use only official taxi queues with green license plates. Never share passport or hotel details with unsolicited strangers. Ask uniformed station staff for directions instead. Use Fukuoka Airport's Subway Namboku Line (¥270) or shuttle bus (¥470). Download Google Maps offline.
scams.location: Hakata Station and Fukuoka Airport taxi stands
